source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-6

procedures.title: Battery specific gravity: read with a hydrometer
steps: Correct each reading to 80°F: add .004 (four points) per 10° above 80°F; subtract .004 per 10° below 80°F.
Example: 1.260 at 110°F corrects to 1.272 (fully charged); 1.272 at 0°F corrects to 1.240 (partly charged).
notes: See figure 7b in the manual: do not draw in too much electrolyte, keep the tube vertical, float free, read at eye level.

procedures.title: Battery: specific gravity cell comparison test
steps: Use this when no instrument tester is available.
Measure the specific gravity of every cell, whatever the state of charge.
If the highest and lowest cells differ by .050 (50 points) or more, replace the battery.

procedures.title: Battery cable terminals: install on posts (Corvette battery installation)
steps: Do not spread the cable terminal open past the position shown in figure 8b, or it takes a permanent set and stays loose.
With the terminal fully open, press it onto the post as far as it will go, at least flush with or below the post top.
Never drive the terminal onto the post with a hammer or other tool.
notes: Figure 8b in the manual shows the Corvette battery seated in its carrier with the hold-down hardware (view B) and the battery cable clipped along the body to the starter solenoid (view A).
